title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear amounts and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction to Iron and Folate in Pregnancy
Iron and folate are two essential nutrients for the health of pregnant women and their babies. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the baby's brain and nervous system. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), daily iron and folate supplementation is crucial for pregnant women.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl
This recipe combines grilled chicken rich in heme iron with vegetables rich in vitamin C, enhancing iron absorption. Ingredients include:
- 100g grilled chicken
- 1 cup cooked white rice
- 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, broccoli)
- 1 lemon
- Salt and pepper

Instructions: Grill chicken for 15 minutes, cook rice and vegetables for 10 minutes. Mix all ingredients together and squeeze lemon juice on top.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Water Spinach Stir-Fry Bowl
This recipe combines beef stir-fry rich in heme iron with water spinach rich in vitamin C. Ingredients include:
- 100g beef stir-fry
- 1 cup cooked white rice
- 1 cup water spinach
- 1 lemon
- Salt and pepper

Instructions: Stir-fry beef for 10 minutes, cook rice and water spinach for 10 minutes. Mix all ingredients together and squeeze lemon juice on top.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Red Bean and Vegetable Bowl
This recipe combines cooked red beans rich in non-heme iron with mixed vegetables rich in vitamin C. Ingredients include:
- 100g cooked red beans
- 1 cup cooked white rice
- 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, broccoli)
- 1 lemon
- Salt and pepper

Instructions: Cook red beans for 20 minutes, cook rice and vegetables for 10 minutes. Mix all ingredients together and squeeze lemon juice on top.

## Food Safety Notes
When cooking for pregnant women, it's essential to consider food safety to avoid food poisoning. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should avoid eating raw or undercooked food, especially meat, eggs, and seafood. Additionally, wash hands and cooking utensils frequently to prevent bacterial contamination.

## Conclusion
These three recipes provide a rich source of iron and folate for pregnant women while ensuring food safety. For a healthy pregnancy, pregnant women should incorporate these recipes into their [meal planner](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner) and consult additional information on [prenatal nutrition](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) on our website.

faqs.question: Why are iron and folate important for pregnant women?
faqs.answer: Iron and folate help create red blood cells and support the development of the baby's brain and nervous system.

faqs.question: How can I increase iron absorption?
faqs.answer: Combine iron with vitamin C, such as eating vitamin C-rich foods like lemons, oranges, or vegetables along with iron-rich foods.

faqs.question: Are there any foods I should avoid during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Yes, pregnant women should avoid eating raw or undercooked food, especially meat, eggs, and seafood, to prevent food poisoning.
